text: Course six already covered the classic mistake: a business rule that updates its own table without excluding the change it just made, so the update triggers the rule again. This lesson is about catching that happening in a live transaction, and fixing it with real code.

A recursive business rule doesn't always look slow one run at a time. Here, calculate priority score fires five times for a single save, at fourteen, fourteen, eleven, nine, and finally zero milliseconds. No single line looks alarming. The tell is the count: one agent clicked save once, and one business rule fired repeatedly, with durations shrinking toward zero as the value it's recalculating finally stops changing.

Here's the usual cause: the business rule computes a priority score, then calls current dot update to save the record again from inside its own script. That's a brand-new save, and ServiceNow treats it exactly like any other update — which makes every business rule configured to run on update, including this one, eligible to fire again.

Two real fixes close this. First, an idempotent guard: compare the new score to the current one, and if nothing actually changed, return without saving at all. Second, current dot setWorkflow false, called right before update, tells the platform this particular save should not re-fire business rules on the table. Together, the record saves once, correctly, and nothing re-triggers because of it.

Three things to carry forward: detect by count, not duration — the same rule name repeated is the signature, even when each run is fast. Diagnose by looking for current dot update inside an after business rule. And confirm the fix the same way lesson five taught — turn on debug business rule, repeat the save, and check the rule now fires exactly once.

With detection and recursive triggers both covered, lesson eight puts everything from this chapter to work in one real scenario: profiling a slow incident update, finding a query stuck inside a loop, and finding a business rule firing six times — then fixing both.
